audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven full-layer stages contradict their own side: Level 1 (Skill), Level 2 and Level 3 (Gnar), First item and 2+ items (Gnar) all carry Akshan-favoured boilerplate about winning trades and taking over the lane.
audit.why: Mini Gnar's Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against your 850, so he genuinely out-ranges you early, and Mega's bulk plus Wallop reclaims the lane at items. The content layer grades it that way; the full layer's stage text never followed.
audit.corrected: Each contradicted stage now names the mechanic that owns it — Boomerang Throw's range at 1, its cooldown refund at 2, Hop's escape at 3, and Mega's Wallop plus HP at the item stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's tracked ability is "GNAR! (Mega)", and every cooldown, do, don't and interactions line is written around the ultimate. The page also called Mega's stun a "W ground-slam AOE stun" without ever naming it.
audit.why: The ability that actually decides this lane is Wallop — Mega Gnar's W, a flat 7s stun on the area in front of him. That is what lands on Heroic Swing, and at 7s it is available in almost every Mega window. GNAR! (90/60/30) is the ultimate, but Riot's description is explicit that only enemies thrown into a wall are stunned, so it is conditional in a way the page never said.
audit.corrected: The tracked ability across the cooldown block, do's, don'ts and interactions report is now Wallop with its 7s cooldown, and GNAR!'s wall condition is stated wherever it appears.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page connected GNAR!'s wall stun to Heroic Swing's terrain requirement.
audit.why: Heroic Swing fires a grapple into terrain, so Akshan has to fight near walls to keep an exit. GNAR! stuns and adds bonus damage to anything it throws into a wall. Those two facts point in opposite directions: the terrain that gives you an escape is the terrain that makes his ultimate lethal. That trade-off is the single most important thing to know here and it was absent.
audit.corrected: The interaction is now written into mid, late, the 2+ items stage and the cooldown block.

edits.before: Out-angle the poke war and execute the chip with R. GNAR! (Mega) is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Out-angle the poke war and execute the chip with R. His Rage bar is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step.

edits.before: Three-hit passive trades win level 1 — boomerang the wave, double-auto the step-up, and back off before the return.
edits.after: His mini Boomerang Throw out-ranges your single Q at level 1 — last-hit at range, don't walk up, and set up level 2.

edits.before: Q max gets the return hit — both boomerang passes on him plus the passive proc is a third of his HP bar.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw is 16s but refunds when he catches it — he kites your Q max rather than trading into it.

edits.before: Full kit: E swing around terrain fires while moving — trades start at angles melee kits literally cannot answer.
edits.after: Hop at 3 lets him bounce off your head and leave — your swing angles never pin a Gnar who won't stand still.

edits.after: Trade on his CS timings and bank the passive shield-sprints. Watch the Rage bar — Wallop is a 7s stun in Mega.

edits.before: First item spike — the swing-fire pattern now removes half bars. Take over the lane and start roaming for revives.

edits.before: Crit items even out the field — your edge stays the map game: revives, executes, and swings nobody wards.
edits.after: Mega tanks your lethality and GNAR! stuns anything it throws into a wall — your edge is the map game.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR! (Mega): matchup-defining — Mega all-in near walls — track his rage bar like a cooldown. Check it before every step-up. - E swing is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Gnar Wallop: matchup-defining — Mega's 7s stun is what catches the swing, and GNAR! only stuns what it throws into a wall. Track the Rage bar. - E swing is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.after: Fill his Rage bar so Mega's W (Wallop) stun, up every 7s, lands on your Heroic Swing

edits.before: This is your window. With E Heroic Swing up you can poke around terrain and its cooldown resets to 0.5s on any champion takedown, while his only hard CC requires mega form. Trade hard while his Rage bar is low, but the moment it fills, disengage — a mega-Gnar W ground-slam stun or his E leap lands on your swing and his big mega autos/boomerang burst you. Never commit E when he's one auto from transforming.
edits.after: This is your window. With E Heroic Swing up you poke around terrain and its cooldown resets to 0.5s on any takedown, while his only hard CC needs Mega form. Trade hard while Rage is low; the moment it fills, disengage — Wallop is a 7s stun that lands on your swing. Note the trap: Heroic Swing needs terrain, and GNAR! stuns whatever it throws into a wall, so your exit walls are his kill walls. Never commit E when he's one auto from transforming.

edits.before: Once mega-Gnar has two items he stops dying to your lethality and his W AOE stun deletes you if your E gets caught mid-swing. Your R execute still threatens him at low HP, but he won't get low — he just tanks and stuns. Close this lane on your Youmuu's spike and take the snowball to other lanes with W camo roams; if it goes long, mega-Gnar reclaims it and you're the squishy one.
edits.after: Once Mega Gnar has two items he stops dying to your lethality and Wallop's 7s stun deletes you if your E gets caught mid-swing. Worse, GNAR! only stuns what it throws into a wall, and Heroic Swing needs terrain to cast — his ult punishes the exact ground you fight on. Your R still threatens him low, but he won't get low; he tanks and stuns. Close this on your Youmuu's spike and roam with W camo.

notes: The packet flagged this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere; Wallop's flat 7s, Boomerang Throw's 16s at rank 1 with its catch refund, and Hop's 22s at rank 1 now give concrete windows. Gnar's Rage bar is not a cooldown and Riot's data gives no decay or fill rate, so nothing numeric was asserted about it — only that it is the clock to read.
